did_you_know.text: Did you know? Baasha, king of Israel, fortified Ramah to prevent the people of Judah from coming and going. Ramah therefore served as a strategic point facing the kingdom of Judah.
Did you know? Asa financed his alliance with Ben-Hadad, king of Aram, with silver and gold taken from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the royal palace.
Did you know? Asa reminded Ben-Hadad that there had been alliances between their royal houses, and he asked him to break his alliance with Baasha in order to relieve the pressure on Judah.

Did you know? Ben-Hadad attacked cities in the northern part of the kingdom of Israel, including Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and the store cities of Naphtali. As a result of the attack, Baasha was forced to stop building Ramah.
Did you know? After Baasha abandoned Ramah, Asa mobilized all Judah. The people dismantled the stones and timber of the fortifications and used them to build Geba and Mizpah.
Did you know? Hanani the seer rebuked Asa not for fighting Baasha, but for relying on the king of Aram instead of relying on the LORD.
Did you know? Hanani reminded Asa of the Cushites and Libyans, who had a vast army with many chariots and horsemen, and said that the LORD had delivered them into Asa’s hand when he relied on him.

Did you know? Hanani described the LORD as one whose eyes range throughout the earth to strengthen those whose hearts are fully committed to him. According to Hanani, Asa’s decision would lead to wars from that time on.
Did you know? Asa did not accept Hanani’s rebuke: he became angry, imprisoned him in the house of the stocks, and mistreated some of the people at that time.
Did you know? In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became diseased in his feet. The account notes that even during his illness he did not seek the LORD, but turned to physicians.
